sentences.text: Wellnhopterus was a mid-sized pterosaur with an estimated wingspan of about 3 meters. Unlike the slender jaws and long neck of Quetzalcoatlus, this animal possessed a blunt snout and a robust, short neck.

The known fossils include a set of jaws, several neck vertebrae, and a fragmentary long bone. These remains show well-defined bluntness in the jaws and a stockier, shorter neck compared to Quetzalcoatlus.
A separate genus named Javelinadactylus was briefly assigned to these fossils in July 2021 before the paper was retracted.
An early reconstruction of Quetzalcoatlus based on these fossils depicted a snout that was too blunt, an error repeated in many popular works.
Its coexistence with larger pterosaurs suggests that pterosaur diversity in the Maastrichtian was higher than previously thought.
Fossils of Wellnhopterus were discovered in the Javelina Formation at Big Bend National Park in Brewster County, Texas. The fossil remains were discovered in March 1986 by preparator Robert Rainey.
The species was formally named and described in December 2021 by Brian Andres and Wann Langston Jr. The genus Wellnhopterus was named by Andres and Langston in 2021.
In 1996, researchers noted the fossils came from older layers than Quetzalcoatlus and featured a shorter snout and neck. In 2013, Brian Andres analyzed the fossils and classified them as azhdarchids.
Only one fossil occurrence of Wellnhopterus has been recorded.
It is likely that Wellnhopterus was a raptorial predator specializing in large prey.

It is classified in the family Azhdarchidae, though its exact position within the group is debated. The 2021 description placed Wellnhopterus within the family Azhdarchidae. The genus is classified within the family Azhdarchidae.

A 2023 study by Rubi Pêgas and colleagues recovered Wellnhopterus in a different position than the original 2021 analysis. Recent analyses place it in a basal position outside the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae, forming a group with Phosphatodraco and Aralazhdarcho.
Wellnhopterus belongs to the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae. Wellnhopterus is a member of the class Reptilia.
Wellnhopterus lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period. This azhdarchid pterosaur lived in what is now Texas, United States.
Wellnhopterus lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
